verdict.rationale: LiteLLM's proxy logs request inputs, outputs and exceptions to many logging destinations, assigns each request a call_id, and keeps tracking request metadata such as spend. This links logged requests to cost, but inspection appears to happen mainly in external logging tools. missing for 10: documented per-request latency and token-count fields on logged entries, a first-party UI or view for browsing logged requests and responses, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can inspect logged requests and responses with latency, token counts, and cost attached

citations.quote: Log Proxy input, output, and exceptions using: Langfuse, OpenTelemetry, GCS, s3, Azure (Blob) Buckets...
